# FleshCore.cfg.txt -- do not edit the ids.
# Q anchor quest local id          P chunk pool local ids
# L cell wound maxcells budget mincells dropcells   H hitmode radius cooldownms
# M shardnames sectionnames         -- 0 0 = built-in; small = force a wrap
# S skinshader tintgain             G goreDiffuse goreNormal
# V trianglesPerLump                 -- how the solid fill is grouped
# C prewarm                          -- 1: build a body when they LOAD
# R reread pollMs roster             -- 1: rebuild a changed 3D off the game's thread.
#   roster: 1 offers every actor this session has seen to the warm thread whenever
#   that thread is idle, so a target a same-cell load raises no event for is built BEFORE
#   something hits them. Otherwise such targets are a large share of game-thread rebuilds.
# K clearGain jointGain headGain     -- the clearance rule; headGain is not used yet (0 = none)
# HD probes swap lock skinGate       -- the head probes, [HEAD] in the log.
#   probes 1 costs about a millisecond on the FIRST wound of each of the first
#   eight targets (read-only). HD 0, as shipped, leaves them off.
# E mode perFrame prime clearance lift -- 0 script places; 1 PROBE (engine places first piece);
#                                       2 engine places all. clearance/lift: as FL_Watch's SpawnClearance/SpawnLift
# NL spell hit player  -- NEVER KILL BY ORIGIN. A wound from an origin
#   marked 1 takes flesh and never counts toward death. player 1 applies this
#   (and a W row's nokill column) to the player too; 0 exempts them. A mod's
#   FL_Api.SetNoKill on an actor outranks both and always applies.
#   W rows take an optional column 15, nokill, after mark: 1 = this wound never
#   kills. Every shipped row has its # comment there, so none sets it.
# PK on key doubleMs effectLocal spellLocal pauseGame  -- THE PANEL
#   NOT `P`: that is the chunk pool's list of local ids, and its parser APPENDS
#   rather than assigns, so a second P row would push a bad record onto the pool.
#   Rows are compared whole at both ends, so PK cannot be read as P.
#   key is a DX scan code and is read by FL_WATCH, not by the DLL: the key is
#   watched in Papyrus, where the engine already refuses to deliver key events
#   while a menu owns the controls. 52 is DIK_PERIOD -- the '.' on the main
#   keyboard; the numpad's is 83. doubleMs is how close two taps must be.
#   effectLocal is the DLL's -- the magic effect it watches for. spellLocal is
#   FL_Watch's -- the spell that carries it. Two records, two numbers.
#   pauseGame 1 pauses the game while the panel has focus; 0 leaves it running.
#   What the panel SETS lives in FleshCore.panel.json beside this file, and is
#   applied over these rows before their range checks run.
# HK on tickMs  -- THE HOOKS' SWITCH AND THE HOOK THREAD'S CADENCE.
#   on 0 turns every T row and every registered row off; the hit path is then
#   the H row alone. tickMs (50..1000, default 100) is how often the
#   hook thread looks for a command file, a vortex, a heal, a tracked blow or an
#   event to relay -- and posts nothing at all when there is nothing to do.
# T type kind thr window form size count cells budget depth layers parts anchor sweep kick mark nokill prio  # name
#   THE TRIGGER TABLE: a blow becomes a wound by ROW.
#   type    what swung: blunt (mace, warhammer, any bash) slash (sword, dagger,
#           axe, greatsword, battleaxe) pierce (bow, crossbow) any
#           kw:<KeywordEditorID> (a keyword on the weapon). unarmed and staff
#           parse and never fire: neither hit voxelises.
#           fire frost shock shout werewolf drain are typed from a HOSTILE
#           effect's record when it lands (resist value, keyword, archetype);
#           mgef:<signed runtime FormID> names one effect.
#           THE WEAPON ITSELF: sword dagger waraxe mace greatsword
#           battleaxe warhammer bow staff crossbow, by the record's animation
#           type (warhammer by its keyword; a bound weapon is the kind its
#           record is). A bash matches no weapon kind; `bash` is
#           its own type -- any weapon or shield swung as a bash.
#   kind    any = every blow of that type; pct = one blow of at least thr per cent of their max health; abs = one blow of at least thr points;
#           per = every blow of that type, and the wound's SIZE is thr units
#           per point of damage (0 < thr <= 10): never under the row's own
#           size, never over 40. On a magic type it never fires on the apply
#           (no damage there): the damage taken over one element cooldown sizes it;
#           winpct / winabs = the damage of that type within `window` seconds
#           (0.5..60), summed on the tick, once per window; drain = thr cells
#           per second for `window` seconds (0.5..120) after each apply of a
#           matching effect, as bites at the row's anchor.
#   window  seconds, for the window kinds and drain; 0 otherwise.
#   form .. nokill are the W row's columns 3-15, same order, same meaning.
#   prio    config rows carry -1 so that any row a mod registers outranks them.
#   ONE WOUND PER BLOW: rows are tried by prio, then a row naming them before
#   one naming everyone, then by threshold descending. Size scales with how
#   far past the threshold the blow was, up to three times (a per row's size
#   is the damage's instead). THE HQ'S COMBAT PAGE builds its own rows
#   -- one per weapon kind and magic type it has switched on, owner HQ, prio 5
#   -- from FleshCore.panel.json, and while it is on these T rows stand down
#   unless its "keep the config's rows" switch is set. Its gates (who may be
#   cut, the health % above which nobody is, the reset clocks) apply to every
#   row of every owner.
#   Damage and health are read from the engine's own HitData and actor values
#   (facts.h, THE BLOW) and cross-checked against the event before they are
#   believed; a blow whose numbers are not believed can only fire `any` rows.
#   A registry `vulnhp` on them declines every blow above that health % here.
#   A registered SCALAR on them (FL_Api.SetScalar) divides every threshold and
#   scales what a blow or a drain does to them -- never a spell or a command.
# D sever severMin severMax rings rigid partSpan lossLimb lossTrunk lossHead
#   sever: 1 forges severed sections into physical pieces; 0 still sweeps,
#   still takes the part off them and still kills them for it -- it only writes no object.
#     headSkinPct headBonePct headBrainPct coalesce coalesceGap sectLumps
#   sectLumps (column 16): lumps of fill a cell a layer a SEVERED SECTION
#   carries; 0 = every lump there is. Shards keep one whole lump a cell.
#   Capping sections at one lump too leaves a severed thigh hollow.
#   Counted in WHOLE lumps of the size the mesh makes them (48 body,
#   108 head fill). Default 8 when the column is absent; clamped 0..64.
#   Columns 11-13 are the head's by-layer death thresholds, in per cent of what they were
#   born with: skin 40, bone 15, brain 25 (0 = any loss at all is fatal). Shipped
#   explicitly only so that columns 14 and 15 can be reached. Skin is
#   40, not lower: an UNDRESSED target has only face skin on their head, no skull and
#   no brain, so at 20 one BisectSkull kills them before the cut can be looked at.
# W effect form size count cells budget depth layers parts anchor sweep kick mark -- one per spell
#   parts:  which parts it may touch, by name ('head', 'left thigh' or the
#           API's one-word key 'lthigh' -- either spelling), comma-
#           separated, '-' = every part; a name the engine does not know is
#           logged and ignored here, refused on a T row or a command
#   anchor: WHERE it lands -- '-'/aim = the crosshair; centre/front/back/
#           top/bottom/left/right = that side of the locked part's live
#           cells, and the aim is not consulted at all
#   sweep:  'nosever' skips the dismemberment sweep for this wound, so what
#           it cuts free stays where it is instead of dropping as a piece
#   kick:   N multiplies the launch force of every piece (0 = the default throw)
#   mark:   what every piece wears -- 0 as they do, 1 blood, 2 alt
#   budget 0 = STRIP (remove it, build nothing); layers 0 = derive from depth
Q	2101
X	2188
K	1.00	1.60	0.00
P	2049,2050,2051,2052,2053,2054,2055,2056,2057,2058,2059,2060,2061,2062,2063,2064,2065,2066,2067,2068
L	4.0	12.0	34	12	34	10
M	0	0
H	0	9.0	900
HD	0	0	0	0
# HF mode -- THEIR OWN FACE. 0 off; 1 READ their live FaceGen
#   face into the lattice as their skin, with nothing drawn changed and nothing
#   of it counting towards their death; 2 as 1, and their face's skin counts
#   towards the head's skin threshold (D row); 3 as 2, AND their face
#   is cut on them like their body's skin -- its skin partition privatised and
#   the survivors written into a new index buffer on the DLL's clone.
HF	3
# FA acc maxVerts -- THEIR EYES, BROWS, MOUTH AND HAIR. acc 0 reads no accessories;
#   acc 1 reads every OTHER BSDynamicTriShape on them -- eyes, brows, mouth,
#   face overlays, hair -- through the same private-buffer reader as their face,
#   but as WARDROBE: layer 0, not skin, forging nothing and counting towards no
#   death rule, and cut by the same Redraw that cuts their body. maxVerts is a
#   COST ceiling, not a filter against physics hair: 12000 admits
#   typical physics wigs (8,000-11,000 vertices) and excludes far denser shapes. See
#   Config::accMaxVerts in flesh.cpp. FA 1 needs HF 3: an accessory is always cut, and
#   below HF 3 their face is not.
FA	1	12000
# FO x y z -- head-bind space to root space, for the shapes above. Measured
#   off the vanilla head node's own local transform and corroborated to about a
#   quarter of a unit by the heads' bounding boxes; overridden by their own face
#   when theirs measured it as a pure translation, and in every case verified
#   against their face's bounding box before anything is built. See Config::headOffset in flesh.cpp.
FO	0.000	-1.548	120.344
# FOM x y z -- the same offset for a MALE BODY. Read off a male high-poly head
#   (malehead.nif, 'NPC Head [Head]' translation -0.000256 -1.547517 120.343590)
#   and off skeleton_male.nif root-to-head: the same three numbers as the female row to
#   the third decimal, kept as its own row because it is a constant of the MALE rig.
FOM	0.000	-1.548	120.344
# DC <mode> <delta> <hold> <bleedX> -- the death camera, written into the
#   player camera's state objects on the game's thread when a wound of theirs
#   posts. delta is added to the third-person zoom offsets, bleedX multiplies
#   the bleedout state's own zoom, and both are put back after hold seconds.
#   In play: state 9 at the wound, state 11 within half
#   a second, bleedout zoom 200 -> 500, and the camera visibly further out.
DC	1	0.35	6	2.5
S	0	1.00
G	Textures\FleshCore\flesh_muscle.dds	Textures\FleshCore\flesh_muscle_n.dds
V	108
C	1
R	1	500	1
#   E 2 (shipped): the engine places every piece on the game's thread at
#   about 0.1-0.2 ms each, their 3D arriving within about 16 ms, every
#   position and rotation as set. The script's own loop costs about 0.2 s PER
#   PIECE -- seconds for a Detonate -- which is the hitch felt
#   when shards spawn. 1 = the engine places the first piece only; 0 = the script places all.
E	2	6	0	14.0	6.0
# PART SPAN (col 7) -- the widest a severed SECTION may be, in JOINTS,
# before it is split into pieces that are not. A bisection otherwise leaves
# an entire side of them as ONE rigid object -- an arm and a leg joined
# through the pelvis -- which reads as a mannequin rather than as gore.
#   thigh <-> hip 1   thigh <-> chest 2   a whole arm 2   a whole leg 2
#   a right hand to a right foot 7
# 2 keeps a whole arm and a whole leg intact and forbids a whole side of the body.
# 1 makes limbs come apart at the elbow and the knee.  0 turns the rule off.
# LOSS DIVISORS (cols 8 and 9) -- a part counts as LOST when
#   cells_now * N < cells_at_birth.   4 = 'under a quarter left',
#   2 = 'under half left'.  Higher N is HARDER to lose.
# A limb is lost by coming OFF, so it asks whether almost none is left.
# The trunk is lost by being DESTROYED, so it asks whether most is gone:
# half a thigh is a terrible wound, half a chest is a death: a target can
# survive with 35 of 87 torso cells and 10 of 31 abdomen cells.
# lossHead (col 10) is its own case: a head is lost by being OPENED, so 1
# means ANY cell of their skull going is fatal. Only something that takes
# BONE empties a cell -- stripping the face leaves the bone and does not
# kill. Raise it if a split skull should be survivable.
# COALESCE (col 14) -- the smallest a severed SECTION may be before it is
#   merged into the nearest section of another part within COALESCE_GAP cells (col 15).
#   Raise-only: a spell whose pieces are already bigger keeps them.
#   COALESCE_GAP (col 15) -- how far apart, in cells, two sections may be and still merge.
D	1	7	6	1	1	2	4	2	2	40	15	25	24	4	8
PK	1	52	300	2242	2243	0
NL	0	0	1
HK	1	100
# ND noDecals -- NO ENGINE DECALS ON FLESHCORE'S OWN GEOMETRY. Bit 1 (1):
#   the fill shapes carry NiAVObject "No Decals" (bit 10, 1024) from the moment
#   the meat is revealed, so a blow's blood splash is not projected onto
#   forty-five skinned shells of fifty thousand triangles each -- the 75-115 ms
#   frame every hit on a revealed target costs without it.
#   Bit 2 (2): the forged pieces' NIFs carry the same flag. 3 = both (shipped);
#   0 = off.
ND	3
# FP frameProbe -- THE FRAME PROBE. 1: one task a frame; after every
#   wound one [FRAME] line says the frame rate before it and the longest frames
#   after it, with offsets on the wound's own clock. 0: off.
FP	1
# RA redrawAsync -- THE REDRAW WORKER. 1: a wound's new index buffers
#   (one per partition of every shape it touched -- thirty to seventy shapes,
#   about 0.2 ms each on the blow's own frame) are
#   gathered and created on a worker thread and installed on the next frame;
#   the cut shows one frame after the blow instead of on it, and the frame the
#   blow lands on no longer pays for it. 0 = off.
#   The restore and re-read paths stay on the game's thread either way.
RA	1
# TE tear -- THE TEAR RULE. A limb tears the rest of the way when a
#   wound has taken this fraction or more of its cross-section at the wound, or
#   of the flesh that joins it to the part it hangs from: a bite wider than the
#   arm cannot leave the arm, and half a shoulder does not hold one. Against
#   what they were born with, so the second bite at a joint tears what the first
#   left. Arms and legs -- and the trunk across a blade's cut: a
#   cleave that leaves standing half of what this lets a limb keep (a quarter at
#   0.5) of their chest and belly where its plane crosses them, with trunk on
#   both sides of it, went through, so the rest of that band tears and the cut
#   reaches past the blade's reach, across the trunk and an arm's thickness
#   beyond. 0 turns it off (a limb then stays until every cell at
#   the joint is gone, and a cleave stops where its reach does).
TE	0.5
# DR effect rate seconds [parts] [anchor] -- A DRAIN SPELL. The effect
#   (a local id in FleshCore.esp) is not a wound but a FEED: while it is on them
#   the tick takes rate cells a second from them, as one bite a second at the
#   anchor of the named parts (a part name or the API's key; '-' = anywhere),
#   for up to seconds after the last apply -- the effect's own script ends it
#   the moment the caster lets go. Never a spell's W row. 2379 is Voxel Drain
#   (0x94B, a copy of the vampire's drain that still absorbs health): a
#   vampire feeds from the neck down, so the chest's top.
DR	2379	4.0	30	chest	top	# Voxel Drain
# AR on reach  hard: slash pierce blunt magic  soft: slash pierce blunt magic
#   cloth: slash pierce blunt magic -- THE ARMOUR, PARSED BUT NOT APPLIED. In this
#   release no wound is weighed against what they wear: physical weapons deal
#   full flesh damage, and these numbers are read and logged but change no
#   wound's size, pieces, depth or threshold damage. What is worn is still classed,
#   for the HQ's tester, by AREA: the cells within `reach` units of the spot that still have their
#   outer layer and hold a worn shape -- a hole cut in a breastplate covers
#   nothing. The hardest class there wins.
#   Classes: hard = heavy armour, and light armour of metal, glass, scales,
#   chitin, stalhrim, bonemold, Nordic or Falmer material; soft = every other
#   light armour (leather, hide, fur, studded); cloth = clothing; jewellery and
#   wigs are none. Families: slash (blades, axes, claws), pierce (arrows, bolts),
#   blunt (maces, hammers, bashes), magic (fire, frost, shock, shouts,
#   drains, staves). The HQ has no Armour card in this release.

# DetonateSelf -- the SAME wound as 2175, on an effect whose spell is
#   delivery = Self. The Shredder spells cast it on the victim FROM the victim,
#   which cannot miss; the aimed 2175 fires a projectile and did, every time.
W	2205	detonate	1.0	1	20	20	3	0	-	-	-	0	0	# DetonateSelf
#
# THE FOUR LIMB CUTS (ArmOffL/R, LegOffL/R): both forearms-and-hands and
#   both lower-legs-and-feet. They are delivery = Self like DecapitateSelf, so
#   Cast(who, who) lands on them instead of firing a bolt along their facing.
#
#   ANCHOR IS centre AND NOT top.
#   Top looks right because the lattice
#   is in skeleton-root BIND space (measured: a shot on a live calf logged at
#   z 29.9, a head at z 110..132) so top would be the elbow and the knee
#   whatever way they are lying when the cut lands. It is not:
#   Anchor::Top is (mean x, mean y, MAX z) -- the centroid in two axes and
#   the top in the third. For the lower legs, which are vertical in bind pose,
#   that is the knee and it would have worked. For a forearm, which is not,
#   the point sits beside the limb rather than on it, and a bite there clips
#   the side of the arm without ever taking a full cross-section.
#   Top would sever two limbs of four and look like a bug in the other two.
#
#   centre is the one anchor that is inside the part no matter how the bind
#   pose holds it, so the radius does the work instead: big enough to swallow
#   the WHOLE named part. That is safe here in a way it is nowhere else,
#   because the parts column bounds what may be taken -- nothing outside the
#   named part is eligible, so a radius larger than the limb cannot eat the
#   upper arm or the thigh. What it does is remove the forearm (or the lower
#   leg) entirely, which leaves the hand (or the foot) attached to nothing:
#   the sever pass then drops it whole, the same way the head drops after
#   neck. A piece of them on the floor, not only a spray.
#
#   16.0 and 22.0 are those parts half-lengths with margin, off a 128-unit
#   bind-space body. Sever stays ON -- a nosever here would take the forearm
#   and leave the hand hanging in the air.
W	2207	bite	16.0	1	14	16	3	0	left forearm	centre	-	0	0	# ArmOffL
W	2209	bite	16.0	1	14	16	3	0	right forearm	centre	-	0	0	# ArmOffR
W	2211	bite	22.0	1	14	16	3	0	left lower leg	centre	-	0	0	# LegOffL
W	2213	bite	22.0	1	14	16	3	0	right lower leg	centre	-	0	0	# LegOffR
#
# TAKE A NAMED LIMB -- twelve aimed spells, 0x8AB..0x8C1.
#   Design note: one spell per limb part -- upper arm, forearm, hand,
#   thigh, calf and foot, each side.
#
#   TWO SHAPES. A joint cut takes the PROXIMAL part with a bite at its own
#   centre, and whatever hangs below it -- attached to nothing now -- is
#   dropped WHOLE by the sever pass: cut the thigh and the entire leg falls.
#   That is the shape of the four limb cuts above. A hand or a foot has nothing
#   distal to drop, so those use `all` with the part named, which removes
#   every cell of it and nothing else -- Form::Everything honours the parts
#   mask (lattice.cpp, C.Alive(mask, parts)).
#
#   THE RADII ARE MEASURED. Each is the greatest distance from
#   that part centroid to any of its own vertices, taken off a BodySlide-built
#   male body -- the mesh the game actually loads -- with every vertex
#   assigned by dominant skin bone:
#       upper arm 13.9   forearm 11.4   thigh 20.3   lower leg 18.2
#   rounded up so the bite swallows the whole part rather than most of it.
#   Oversizing is safe because the parts column bounds what may be taken.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LP maxLive shardLife sectionLife -- THE LIVE-PIECE CAP. At most maxLive pieces
#   (shards and severed sections together, every target's) lie about at once; a new
#   one born over that evicts the OLDEST first. shardLife / sectionLife are the
#   seconds a shard / a severed section stays (FL_Chunk's own defaults are 45 / 300).
#   Read by FL_Watch on every load and handed to FL_Chunk through StorageUtil
#   (FC_maxpieces, FC_shardlife, FC_sectionlife); the DLL validates and logs the row.
#   maxLive 0 = no cap.
#   the HQ's "Pieces kept on the ground" slider (Engine page) overrides maxLive
#   once moved (FleshCore.pieces.txt, empty until then, so this row stands on every load);
#   lowering it clears down within seconds. A wound is cut to one piece only at twice the cap.
#   maxLive 35 by default.
LP	35	45	300
# CL bladeAxis combatSeverMax cleaveHalf cleaveReach -- THE CLEAVE. A blow's slab
#   is thin (cleaveHalf cells either side of the plane) and the longest blade's
#   cut reaches cleaveReach UNITS from the impact in the plane of the swing, so one
#   stroke is a cut through the part it struck, not an eight-row band across the whole body (a band that let one greatsword blow at the Gorefest preset take twelve named parts).
#   A greatsword takes all of it, a battleaxe half, a sword 0.3, a war axe 0.25, a
#   dagger 0.2. 0 = across the whole body. In units, not cells: in cells, at
#   cell 8 the reach would be wider than the body.
#   combatSeverMax bounds the severed sections one BLOW may make (spells keep D's).
#   bladeAxis: which WEAPON-node axis is the blade's FLAT (the swing plane's
#   normal): -1 = off (the plane stays horizontal, like a spell's slab),
#   0/1/2 = that local axis. Read it from the "[HIT]   swing plane:"
#   log lines, then set it here.
CL	2	3	0.75	40
# WD defer maxMs perFrame -- THE DEFERRED WOUND. A blow on a target whose lattice is
#   cold (a Restore forgot them) or stale (FL_Watch just dressed them) would
#   voxelise them ON THE BLOW'S FRAME -- a few hundred ms each, more with two targets hit
#   in one frame. defer 1: such a blow, typed effect or drain hands them to
#   the re-read worker and the wound is cut the moment their rebuild lands, off the
#   frame; 2: every origin; 0: off (voxelise on the blow's frame). maxMs: a wound still waiting after
#   this is dropped and says so. perFrame (WD 0 only, needs FP 1): synchronous
#   voxelises one frame may run.
WD	1	1500	1
